cues.text: Averaging means adding to a trade, to change your average price.
cues.say: Averaging means adding to a trade, to change your average price.

cues.text: You buy 1 lot of gold at $4,000. Every $1 move = $100.
cues.say: You buy one lot of gold at four thousand. Every dollar move is a hundred dollars.
Gold drops forty dollars. You're four thousand down.

cues.text: You buy twice your position: 2 more lots at $3,960.
cues.say: So you buy twice your position. Two more lots.

cues.text: With 3 lots, your average price is $3,973.33.
cues.say: With three lots, your average price drops to about three nine seven three.

cues.text: To break even, gold now only needs +$13.33, not +$40.
cues.say: Now gold only needs to rise about thirteen dollars to break even, not forty.
Each dollar is now worth three hundred.
The rule: the move you need, is your loss, divided by your lots, times a hundred.
Two lots, twenty dollars. Three lots, thirteen. Four lots, ten.

cues.text: But if gold falls another $20, you're $10,000 down.
cues.say: But if gold falls another twenty dollars, you're ten thousand down.

cues.text: Set a maximum size and a stop loss first.
cues.say: So set a maximum size, and a stop loss, first.
